name: Chapter 6: Electromagnetic Induction
description: Faraday’s experiments, flux, Faraday’s and Lenz’s laws, motional emf, mutual and self inductance, magnetic energy, ac generator

cards.term: Who showed around 1830 that changing magnetic fields induce currents in closed coils?
cards.definition: Michael Faraday (England) and Joseph Henry (USA)

cards.term: Define electromagnetic induction.
cards.definition: Generation of an emf / current in a circuit by a changing magnetic flux through it

cards.term: Which two devices came directly from Faraday and Henry’s work?
cards.definition: Generators and transformers

cards.term: Experiment 6.1: N-pole pushed towards a coil joined to a galvanometer. What happens?
cards.definition: The pointer deflects while the magnet moves; no deflection when it is held still

cards.term: Experiment 6.1: what happens when the magnet is pulled away, or the S-pole is used?
cards.definition: Deflection reverses for withdrawing; S-pole gives the opposite deflection to N-pole for the same motion

cards.term: Effect of moving the magnet faster?
cards.definition: Larger deflection: a larger rate of change of flux gives a larger emf and current

cards.term: Magnet fixed, coil moved instead. Result?
cards.definition: Same effects: only the relative motion matters

cards.term: Experiment 6.2: coil C₂ (with battery) moved towards coil C₁. Result?
cards.definition: Current is induced in C₁ (reverses when C₂ moves away). C₂’s steady current acts like a bar magnet

cards.term: Experiment 6.3: coils held fixed, key K pressed or released. What is observed?
cards.definition: Momentary deflection on making and (opposite) on breaking; none while K is held closed

cards.term: Experiment 6.3: effect of inserting an iron rod along the coils?
cards.definition: Deflection increases dramatically: iron concentrates the flux

cards.term: Key idea of all three experiments?
cards.definition: Steady flux, however large, induces nothing. Only a changing flux does

cards.term: Example 6.1(a): three ways to get a larger deflection in Experiment 6.2?
cards.definition: Soft-iron core in C₂; more powerful battery; move the arrangement faster

cards.term: Example 6.1(b): show induced current without a galvanometer?
cards.definition: Replace it with a small torch bulb: it glows during relative motion

cards.term: Magnetic flux through a plane area A in a uniform B?
cards.definition: \( \Phi_B = \vec B\cdot\vec A = BA\cos\theta \), θ = angle between B and the area vector (normal)

cards.term: Flux through a curved surface or non-uniform field?
cards.definition: \( \Phi_B = \int \vec B\cdot d\vec A = \sum \vec B_i\cdot d\vec A_i \)

cards.term: Unit and nature of magnetic flux?
cards.definition: weber (Wb = T m²); a scalar

cards.term: Flux is maximum and zero when?
cards.definition: Max BA at θ = 0° (plane ⊥ B). Zero at θ = 90° (plane ∥ B, field lines in the plane)

cards.term: Trap: θ in Φ = BA cos θ is the angle between B and what?
cards.definition: The normal to the plane, not the plane itself. If given the angle with the plane, use sin

cards.term: Three ways to change the flux through a loop?
cards.definition: Change B, change the area A (shrink or stretch), change the angle θ (rotate)

cards.term: State Faraday’s law of induction.
cards.definition: The magnitude of the induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit

cards.term: Mathematical form of Faraday’s law? Coil of N turns?
cards.definition: \( \varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\Phi_B}{dt} \); for N turns \( \varepsilon = -N\dfrac{d\Phi_B}{dt} \) (Φ per turn)

cards.term: What does the negative sign stand for?
cards.definition: The direction of the induced emf (Lenz’s law): it opposes the flux change

cards.term: Induced current in a closed loop of resistance R?
cards.definition: \( I = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{R} = -\dfrac{N}{R}\dfrac{d\Phi_B}{dt} \)

cards.term: Teacher addition: charge that flows through the loop when flux changes by ΔΦ?
cards.definition: \( q = \int I\,dt = \dfrac{N\,\Delta\Phi}{R} \): independent of how fast the flux changes

cards.term: Why is the total induced emf in a coil of N turns N times larger?
cards.definition: Each turn sees the same flux change; the emfs add in series. Hence more turns → more emf

cards.term: Faraday explained Experiment 6.3 how?
cards.definition: Pressing K raises C₂’s current, so flux through C₁ rises → emf. Steady current: flux constant → none. Releasing K: flux falls → emf of opposite sign

cards.term: Induced emf when B decreases (Example 6.2)
cards.definition: ε ≈ 1.0 mV, I = 2 mA

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Example 6.2 · decreasing field

Find the missing step.

Square loop of side 10 cm, R = 0.5 Ω. B = 0.10 T at 45° to the loop’s area vector falls to zero uniformly in 0.70 s. Find emf and I.
  1. ?
  2. Φ₂ = 0, so ΔΦ = 7.1 × 10⁻⁴ Wb
  3. |ε| = ΔΦ/Δt = 7.1 × 10⁻⁴/0.7 ≈ 1.0 mV
  4. I = ε/R = 1.0 × 10⁻³/0.5 = 2 mA
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 6.2 · decreasing field

Find the missing step.

Square loop of side 10 cm, R = 0.5 Ω. B = 0.10 T at 45° to the loop’s area vector falls to zero uniformly in 0.70 s. Find emf and I.
  1. Φ₁ = BA cos 45° = 0.1 × 10⁻² × 0.707 = 7.1 × 10⁻⁴ Wb
  2. Φ₂ = 0, so ΔΦ = 7.1 × 10⁻⁴ Wb
  3. |ε| = ΔΦ/Δt = 7.1 × 10⁻⁴/0.7 ≈ 1.0 mV
  4. I = ε/R = 1.0 × 10⁻³/0.5 = 2 mA

cards.term: Example 6.2: does Earth’s magnetic field also add an emf?
cards.definition: No: it is steady over the experiment, so its flux does not change

cards.term: Flipping a coil in Earth’s field (Example 6.3)
cards.definition: ε ≈ 3.8 mV, I ≈ 1.9 mA

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Example 6.3 · coil flipped

Find the missing step.

Circular coil, r = 10 cm, N = 500, R = 2 Ω, plane ⊥ horizontal B = 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ T. Turned through 180° about a vertical diameter in 0.25 s. Estimate emf and I.
  1. Φ_initial = BA cos 0° = 3 × 10⁻⁵ × π × 10⁻² = 3π × 10⁻⁷ Wb
  2. ?
  3. ε = NΔΦ/Δt = 500 × 6π × 10⁻⁷/0.25 ≈ 3.8 × 10⁻³ V
  4. I = ε/R ≈ 1.9 mA (average value)
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 6.3 · coil flipped

Find the missing step.

Circular coil, r = 10 cm, N = 500, R = 2 Ω, plane ⊥ horizontal B = 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ T. Turned through 180° about a vertical diameter in 0.25 s. Estimate emf and I.
  1. Φ_initial = BA cos 0° = 3 × 10⁻⁵ × π × 10⁻² = 3π × 10⁻⁷ Wb
  2. Φ_final = BA cos 180° = −3π × 10⁻⁷ Wb, so |ΔΦ| = 6π × 10⁻⁷ Wb
  3. ε = NΔΦ/Δt = 500 × 6π × 10⁻⁷/0.25 ≈ 3.8 × 10⁻³ V
  4. I = ε/R ≈ 1.9 mA (average value)

cards.term: Trap in Example 6.3: why does a 180° flip give ΔΦ = 2BA, not zero?
cards.definition: Flux changes sign, +BA → −BA, so |ΔΦ| = 2BA

cards.term: State Lenz’s law.
cards.definition: The polarity of the induced emf is such that it tends to produce a current which opposes the change in flux that produced it

cards.term: What does the minus sign of Faraday’s law express?
cards.definition: Lenz’s law

cards.term: Lenz’s law opposes the ______, not the ______.
cards.definition: Opposes the change in flux, not the flux itself (a decreasing flux is supported, not opposed)

cards.term: N-pole of a magnet approaches a closed coil. Induced current direction and pole faced?
cards.definition: Anticlockwise as seen from the magnet’s side; the coil face acts as an N-pole (repels the magnet)

cards.term: N-pole withdrawn from a coil. Induced current?
cards.definition: Clockwise (seen from the magnet); near face is a S-pole, attracts the receding magnet

cards.term: Quick rule for the coil face nearest an approaching or receding pole?
cards.definition: Approach → same pole (repel); recede → opposite pole (attract). Both oppose the motion

cards.term: Intuition: how can you remember Lenz’s law?
cards.definition: Nature is “lazy”: it resists change. Flux up → induced field points against B. Flux down → induced field points along B

cards.term: Direction of the current in an open circuit?
cards.definition: None flows, but an emf still appears across the open ends, with polarity given by Lenz’s law

cards.term: Why must Lenz’s law hold? (energy argument)
cards.definition: If the induced current aided the change, the magnet would accelerate itself: perpetual motion, violating conservation of energy

cards.term: Where does the work done pulling the magnet against repulsion go?
cards.definition: Into Joule heating in the coil (I²R losses)

cards.term: Example 6.4: Fig 6.7(i): rectangular loop moving into a field pointing into the page. Direction of I?
cards.definition: Flux increases, so induced current is anticlockwise as needed: along bcdab

cards.term: Example 6.4: triangular loop (ii) moving out of the field, and irregular loop (iii)?
cards.definition: Flux decreases in both, so current supports it. (ii) along bacb, (iii) along cdabc

cards.term: Example 6.4: when is there no induced current?
cards.definition: While the loop is completely inside or completely outside the field: flux is constant

cards.term: Example 6.5(a): stationary closed loop between fixed strong magnets. Can it carry current?
cards.definition: No: flux must change; strength alone does nothing

cards.term: Example 6.5(b): closed loop moves normal to a constant E between capacitor plates. Current?
cards.definition: None in both cases (wholly or partly inside): changing electric flux does not induce current here

cards.term: Example 6.5(c): a rectangular and a circular loop leave a uniform B at constant speed. Which has constant emf?
cards.definition: Rectangular: its area inside changes at a constant rate. The circle’s rate varies

cards.term: Example 6.5(d): polarity of the capacitor plates in Fig 6.9?
cards.definition: Plate A is positive with respect to B (approaching magnets raise the flux; Lenz’s law sets the sense)

cards.term: Rod PQ (length l) slides at speed v in a uniform B ⊥ the circuit. Flux and emf?
cards.definition: Φ = Blx, so \( \varepsilon = -\dfrac{d(Blx)}{dt} = Blv \) (motional emf)

cards.term: Motional emf from the Lorentz force?
cards.definition: Force on a charge = qvB along the rod. Work carrying it across l: W = qvBl, so \( \varepsilon = \dfrac{W}{q} = Blv \)

cards.term: Condition for ε = Blv?
cards.definition: B, l and v mutually perpendicular. In general \( \varepsilon = (\vec v\times\vec B)\cdot\vec l \)

cards.term: Trap: rod moves parallel to B, or the rod is parallel to v. Emf?
cards.definition: Zero: the rod does not cut field lines. Only the component ⊥ to both counts

cards.term: If the field is uniform and the rod slides, why is emf across it Blv even without a closed circuit?
cards.definition: Lorentz force separates charge to the ends until qE = qvB; the ends stay at potential difference Blv

cards.term: Which end of the rod is at higher potential?
cards.definition: The end towards which the force on positive charges (q v × B) pushes; current inside the rod flows from low to high potential (source)

cards.term: Teacher addition: rod PQ on rails of resistance R pulled at constant v. Current, force and power?
cards.definition: I = Blv/R; magnetic drag \( F = BIl = \dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R} \); power = Fv = \( \dfrac{B^2l^2v^2}{R} \) = I²R (mechanical → heat)

cards.term: Why is there a magnetic force opposing the rod (Lenz’s law in disguise)?
cards.definition: The induced current in a field feels F = I l × B opposing v; otherwise energy would be created

cards.term: Faraday’s law when the conductor is stationary and B changes: which force acts on the charges?
cards.definition: Only qE (v = 0): a time-varying magnetic field creates an electric field, unlike an electrostatic one

cards.term: How does the induced E-field differ from an electrostatic E?
cards.definition: Its field lines form closed loops; it is non-conservative (∮E·dl = −dΦ/dt ≠ 0)

cards.term: Fundamental significance of Faraday’s discovery?
cards.definition: A moving magnet or changing B exerts force on a stationary charge: electricity and magnetism are related

cards.term: Example 6.6: rod of length R rotating at ω about one end in a field B ⊥ its plane. Emf between centre and rim?
cards.definition: \( \varepsilon = \tfrac12 B\omega R^2 \), from \( \int_0^R B\omega r\,dr \) (mean speed ωR/2)

cards.term: Example 6.6: second method for the rotating rod?
cards.definition: Rate of area swept: dA/dt = ½R²ω, so \( \varepsilon = B\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \tfrac12 B\omega R^2 \)

cards.term: Example 6.6: R = 1 m, 50 rev/s, B = 1 T. Emf?
cards.definition: ½ × 1 × (2π × 50) × 1² = ≈ 157 V

cards.term: Example 6.7: wheel with 10 spokes of 0.5 m, 120 rev/min, H_E = 0.4 G. Emf between axle and rim?
cards.definition: ½ω B R² = ½ × 4π × 0.4 × 10⁻⁴ × 0.25 = 6.28 × 10⁻⁵ V. The 10 spokes are in parallel, so their number does not matter

cards.term: Trap: which component of Earth’s field induces emf in a spinning wheel or falling wire?
cards.definition: The component perpendicular to the plane of motion (vertical for a wheel in a horizontal plane; horizontal for a wire falling east–west)

cards.term: Flux linkage for a closely wound coil of N turns?
cards.definition: NΦ_B (proportional to the current I)

cards.term: Define inductance. Unit and dimensions?
cards.definition: Ratio of flux linkage to current: NΦ/I. Unit henry (H) = Wb/A; [ML²T⁻²A⁻²]. It is a scalar

cards.term: Dimensions of flux? Of emf?
cards.definition: Flux: [ML²T⁻²A⁻¹]; emf: [ML²T⁻³A⁻¹]

cards.term: Inductance depends on what? Analogy?
cards.definition: Geometry and intrinsic material properties only (like capacitance: area, separation, dielectric constant)

cards.term: Define mutual inductance M₁₂.
cards.definition: Flux linkage in coil 1 per unit current in coil 2: \( N_1\Phi_1 = M_{12}I_2 \)

cards.term: Mutual inductance of two long coaxial solenoids (inner radius r₁, length l)?
How is this derived?
cards.definition: B₂ = μ₀n₂I₂ (outer). Flux linkage with inner: N₁Φ = (n₁l)(πr₁²)(μ₀n₂I₂), so M = μ₀n₁n₂πr₁²l

cards.term: Relation between M₁₂ and M₂₁?
cards.definition: M₁₂ = M₂₁ = M (general result, shown here for coaxial solenoids)

cards.term: Why is M₁₂ = M₂₁ useful?
cards.definition: Compute whichever flux is easy (small coil inside a big one: uniform field) and use the equality for the hard direction

cards.term: Solenoids filled with a medium of relative permeability μᵣ. Mutual inductance?
What else does M depend on for a pair of coils?
cards.definition: Their separation and relative orientation

cards.term: Example 6.8: concentric coils, r₁ ≪ r₂. Mutual inductance?
cards.definition: \( M_{12} = M_{21} = \dfrac{\mu_0\pi r_1^2}{2r_2} \) (B₂ = μ₀I₂/2r₂ taken uniform over the small coil)

cards.term: EMF induced in coil 1 when the current in coil 2 varies?
cards.definition: \( \varepsilon_1 = -M\dfrac{dI_2}{dt} \)

cards.term: Teacher addition: coupling coefficient k?
cards.definition: \( M = k\sqrt{L_1L_2} \), 0 ≤ k ≤ 1; k = 1 for perfect flux linkage

cards.term: Define self-induction and self-inductance L.
cards.definition: Emf induced in a coil by its own changing current. \( N\Phi_B = LI \)

cards.term: Self-induced emf?
cards.definition: \( \varepsilon = -L\dfrac{dI}{dt} \): it opposes any increase or decrease of current (“back emf”)

cards.term: Self-inductance of a long solenoid (area A, length l, n turns per length)?
cards.definition: \( L = \mu_0 n^2 A l \); with a core \( L = \mu_r\mu_0 n^2 A l \)

cards.term: Derive L of a solenoid.
cards.definition: B = μ₀nI; N = nl. NΦ = (nl)(μ₀nI)A = μ₀n²AlI, so L = NΦ/I = μ₀n²Al

cards.term: Teacher addition: L in terms of total turns N?
cards.definition: \( L = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l} \): L ∝ N². Doubling the turns (same length) quadruples L

cards.term: Physical role of self-inductance?
cards.definition: Electrical inertia: analogue of mass in mechanics; opposes growth and decay of current

cards.term: Energy needed to build up current I in an inductor?
cards.definition: \( W = \int LI\,dI = \tfrac12 LI^2 \) (analogue of ½mv²)

cards.term: Where is that energy stored?
cards.definition: In the magnetic field (magnetic potential energy)

cards.term: Two coils carrying currents together: emf in coil 1?
cards.definition: \( \varepsilon_1 = -L_1\dfrac{dI_1}{dt} - M_{12}\dfrac{dI_2}{dt} \) (M₁₁ = L₁ is self-inductance)

cards.term: Example 6.9(a): magnetic energy stored in a solenoid in terms of B, A, l?
cards.definition: \( U_B = \dfrac{1}{2}LI^2 = \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0}Al \), using I = B/μ₀n and L = μ₀n²Al

cards.term: Energy density of a magnetic field?
cards.definition: \( u_B = \dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0} \), valid for any region with a B-field, not just a solenoid

cards.term: Magnetic vs electric energy density?
cards.definition: u_B = B²/2μ₀ and u_E = ½ε₀E²: both ∝ (field)²

cards.term: Teacher addition: why does a spark appear when a circuit with a big coil is broken?
cards.definition: Current falls fast: large dI/dt gives a big back emf (L·dI/dt) that can exceed the supply and ionise air across the switch

cards.term: Teacher addition: LR growth and decay in one line?
cards.definition: Current in an LR circuit changes over time constant τ = L/R; the inductor opposes an instantaneous change. Not in NCERT text but often asked

cards.term: Teacher addition: inductors in series (no coupling) and in parallel?
cards.definition: Series: L = L₁ + L₂. Parallel: 1/L = 1/L₁ + 1/L₂

cards.term: What does an ac generator do?
cards.definition: Converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction

cards.term: Basic parts of an ac generator?
cards.definition: Armature coil on a rotor shaft, uniform B from magnets, slip rings and carbon brushes to the external circuit

cards.term: Role of slip rings and brushes?
cards.definition: They connect the rotating coil to the fixed external circuit without twisting the wires

cards.term: Rotating coil: flux at time t? (θ = ωt, θ = 0 at t = 0)
cards.definition: \( \Phi_B = BA\cos\omega t \)

cards.term: Instantaneous emf of a coil of N turns rotating in B?
cards.definition: \( \varepsilon = NBA\omega\sin\omega t = \varepsilon_0\sin\omega t \), ε₀ = NBAω

cards.term: Same emf in terms of frequency ν?
cards.definition: \( \varepsilon = \varepsilon_0\sin 2\pi\nu t,\quad \varepsilon_0 = NBA(2\pi\nu) \)

cards.term: When is the emf maximum and when zero?
cards.definition: Max at θ = 90°, 270° (plane ∥ B, flux changes fastest). Zero at 0°, 180° (plane ⊥ B, flux extreme)

cards.term: Intuition: emf is zero when flux is maximum. Why?
cards.definition: ε = −dΦ/dt: at the peak of cos ωt the slope is zero. Flux and emf are 90° out of phase

cards.term: Trap: if the coil starts parallel to B (θ = 90° at t = 0), what is ε(t)?
cards.definition: ε = ε₀ cos ωt. Always check the position at t = 0

cards.term: What sets the frequency of the emf?
cards.definition: The coil’s rotation frequency ν. Mains frequency: 50 Hz in India, 60 Hz in USA

cards.term: Three ways to raise ε₀?
cards.definition: Increase N, B, A or ω

cards.term: Types of commercial generator by energy source?
cards.definition: Hydro-electric (falling water), thermal (steam from coal etc.), nuclear (nuclear fuel)

cards.term: In most large generators, which part rotates?
cards.definition: The electromagnets; the coils stay stationary. Modern units reach ~500 MW (about 5 million 100 W bulbs)

cards.term: Correction: NCERT calls Nikola Tesla “Yugoslav” and credits him with the machine. Better?
cards.definition: Loose: Tesla (born in what is now Croatia) developed polyphase ac systems and the induction motor. Simple alternators go back to Pixii (1832). Exams just say Tesla

cards.term: Kamla’s bicycle generator (Example 6.10)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Example 6.10 · peak emf

Find the missing step.

Coil of 100 turns, A = 0.10 m², rotating at 0.5 rev/s in B = 0.01 T ⊥ the axis. Maximum emf?
  1. ε₀ = NBAω with ω = 2πν
  2. ?
  3. ε₀ = 100 × 0.01 × 0.1 × 3.14 = 0.314 V
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 6.10 · peak emf

Find the missing step.

Coil of 100 turns, A = 0.10 m², rotating at 0.5 rev/s in B = 0.01 T ⊥ the axis. Maximum emf?
  1. ε₀ = NBAω with ω = 2πν
  2. ω = 2π × 0.5 = π rad/s ≈ 3.14 rad/s
  3. ε₀ = 100 × 0.01 × 0.1 × 3.14 = 0.314 V

cards.term: Points to ponder: which principle does the conservation of energy demand in a closed circuit?
cards.definition: Induced currents flow so as to oppose the flux change (Lenz’s law)

cards.term: Points to ponder: how is an open-circuit emf related to the flux change?
cards.definition: Still ε = −dΦ/dt for the loop; just no current flows

cards.term: Points to ponder: moving charge in a static B vs static charge in a changing B?
cards.definition: Both give emf: a symmetric situation hinting at the principle of relativity behind Faraday’s law

cards.term: Correction: Points to Ponder refers to motional emf in “Section 6.5”. Which?
cards.definition: Section 6.6 (6.5 is Lenz’s law)

cards.term: Note: eddy currents in this chapter now?
cards.definition: No: removed from rationalised NCERT, but JEE, NEET and boards still ask them: currents induced in a bulk conductor by changing flux; used in induction furnaces, damping, magnetic braking

cards.term: Note: LR circuit and transformer here?
cards.definition: Not in this chapter: the transformer comes in Ch 7; LR growth/decay is in JEE though

cards.term: NCERT quantity table
cards.definition: Magnetic flux Φ_B: Wb; [ML²T⁻²A⁻¹]; EMF ε: V; [ML²T⁻³A⁻¹]; Mutual inductance M: H; [ML²T⁻²A⁻²]; Self inductance L: H; [ML²T⁻²A⁻²]

cards.term: Exercise 6.1(a): direction of induced current as the magnet approaches the coil pq (Fig 6.15a)?
cards.definition: Along q → r → p → q

cards.term: Exercise 6.1(b): Fig 6.15(b) with two coils, magnet moving between them. Directions?
cards.definition: Coil pq: along prq; coil xy: along yzx

cards.term: Exercise 6.1(c): tapping key just closed. Direction in the other loop (x, y, z)?
cards.definition: Along y → z → x

cards.term: Exercise 6.1(d): rheostat setting being changed. Direction?
cards.definition: Along z → y → x

cards.term: Exercise 6.1(e): tapping key just released. Direction?
cards.definition: Along x → r → y

cards.term: Exercise 6.1(f): loop around a straight wire with decreasing current. Direction?
cards.definition: No induced current: the wire’s field circles lie in the plane of the loop, so flux is zero

cards.term: Exercise 6.1: general method for these?
cards.definition: (1) Direction of B through the loop. (2) Is flux rising or falling? (3) Induced field opposes rise, supports fall. (4) Right-hand rule for the current

cards.term: Exercise 6.2(a): irregular wire pulled into a circle in a field into the page. Direction?
cards.definition: Area (flux) increases, so induced B points out: anticlockwise, a → d → c → b → a

cards.term: Exercise 6.2(b): circle deformed into a narrow strip, field out of the page. Direction?
cards.definition: Flux decreases, induced B also out: anticlockwise, a′ → d′ → c′ → b′

cards.term: Correction: the answer key writes 6.2(a) as “adcd”. What is right?
cards.definition: Typo: the loop has four labelled points, so the path is a → d → c → b → a (anticlockwise)

cards.term: Induced emf in a small loop inside a solenoid (Exercise 6.3)

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Exercise 6.3 · solenoid and small loop

Find the missing step.

Solenoid, 15 turns/cm. Small loop of area 2.0 cm² inside, normal to the axis. I changes 2.0 A → 4.0 A in 0.1 s. Induced emf?
  1. ?
  2. B = μ₀nI, so ε = μ₀nA(dI/dt), dI/dt = 20 A/s
  3. ε = 4π × 10⁻⁷ × 1500 × 2 × 10⁻⁴ × 20
  4. ε ≈ 7.5 × 10⁻⁶ V
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Exercise 6.3 · solenoid and small loop

Find the missing step.

Solenoid, 15 turns/cm. Small loop of area 2.0 cm² inside, normal to the axis. I changes 2.0 A → 4.0 A in 0.1 s. Induced emf?
  1. n = 15 × 100 = 1500 m⁻¹
  2. B = μ₀nI, so ε = μ₀nA(dI/dt), dI/dt = 20 A/s
  3. ε = 4π × 10⁻⁷ × 1500 × 2 × 10⁻⁴ × 20
  4. ε ≈ 7.5 × 10⁻⁶ V

cards.term: Exercise 6.4(a): 8 cm × 2 cm loop with a cut leaves a 0.3 T field at 1 cm/s, normal to the longer side. Emf and duration?
cards.definition: ε = Blv = 0.3 × 0.08 × 0.01 = 2.4 × 10⁻⁴ V; lasts 2 cm ÷ 1 cm/s = 2 s

cards.term: Exercise 6.4(b): same loop moving normal to the shorter side?
cards.definition: ε = 0.3 × 0.02 × 0.01 = 0.6 × 10⁻⁴ V; lasts 8 cm ÷ 1 cm/s = 8 s

cards.term: Trap: in Exercise 6.4 which side cuts the field lines?
cards.definition: Only the side perpendicular to v and still in the field: length l = 8 cm in (a), 2 cm in (b). Emf lasts as long as the loop is partly in the field

cards.term: Exercise 6.5: 1.0 m rod rotated at 400 rad/s about one end in B = 0.5 T. Emf?
cards.definition: ½BωR² = ½ × 0.5 × 400 × 1 = 100 V

cards.term: Emf in a falling wire (Exercise 6.6)
cards.definition: 1.5 mV, W → E, eastern end higher

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Exercise 6.6 · falling wire

Find the missing step.

10 m east–west horizontal wire falls at 5.0 m/s. B_H = 0.30 × 10⁻⁴ T. (a) emf, (b) direction, (c) which end is higher?
  1. ε = Blv = 0.30 × 10⁻⁴ × 10 × 5.0 = 1.5 × 10⁻³ V
  2. ?
  3. Force on positive charges is eastward, so emf is directed west → east
  4. The eastern end is at higher potential
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Exercise 6.6 · falling wire

Find the missing step.

10 m east–west horizontal wire falls at 5.0 m/s. B_H = 0.30 × 10⁻⁴ T. (a) emf, (b) direction, (c) which end is higher?
  1. ε = Blv = 0.30 × 10⁻⁴ × 10 × 5.0 = 1.5 × 10⁻³ V
  2. v is down, B horizontal north: v × B points east
  3. Force on positive charges is eastward, so emf is directed west → east
  4. The eastern end is at higher potential

cards.term: Exercise 6.7: current falls 5.0 A → 0 in 0.1 s; average induced emf 200 V. Self-inductance?
cards.definition: L = ε/|dI/dt| = 200/(5/0.1) = 4 H

cards.term: Exercise 6.8: M = 1.5 H; current in one coil goes 0 → 20 A in 0.5 s. Change of flux linkage in the other?
cards.definition: ΔNΦ = MΔI = 1.5 × 20 = 30 Wb
